methodology.eligibility: All 20 movie and 19 TV provider/variant identities; Gallic movie-only. Four original titles repeated in A and B; Shrek and Severance added in B.
methodology.success: Raw schema-3 success: requested source identity, actual decoded video, approximately 5 seconds continuous advancement followed by approximately 15 seconds steady playback, within a 60-second total trial deadline.
methodology.firstFrame: Milliseconds from navigation, including resolution, to actual first decoded frame. Successful attempts only; failed first-frame and dimensions are null, never zero.
methodology.percentiles: Median is the usual middle value or mean of the middle pair. Observed p90 is nearest rank ceil(0.9*n). Small samples do not establish population tail latency.
methodology.failurePenalty: Failure-aware mean startup loss assigns 60000 ms to each unsuccessful attempt. This is a decision penalty, not observed wait duration; HTTP 424 failures usually ended earlier.
methodology.weighting: Raw attempt fractions weight repeated original titles twice. Equal-title mean success fraction gives each distinct eligible title one vote; neither is a population uptime estimate.
methodology.quality: Compare decoded dimensions within the same title and round. Film cropping is not a quality penalty. Actual raster, captured ladder declarations and perceived fidelity are separate.
methodology.stability: Use steady-window event/frame deltas. Waiting and stalled events are not added because they can describe the same interruption. Missing steady data on failures remains null.
methodology.cache: Verified deployed code bypasses StreamArena resolved-embed cache reads and writes for admin provider benchmark requests; upstream/CDN and helper asset caches are uncontrolled. This later verified metadata clarifies the generic raw options.serverCachePolicy label; it does not claim a fully cold origin or CDN.
methodology.speed: B forces and records playbackRate=1. A did not record playbackRate; successful media-time/wall-time window ratios confirm approximately normal-speed advancement.
methodology.unavailableGroup: All 18 zero-success identities are tied with no verified playback; no quality or successful-start speed ranking is assigned.
methodology.selection: Preserve explicit source pins and existing automatic/manual eligibility and language hints. The backend default uses source metadata and health; it does not choose the provider with the highest supported requested resolution. In-player quality controls remain separate. Priority weights are operating policy, not measured scores.
methodology.separateValidation: Resume at 300 seconds and 120-second endurance are complete in the separate analysis-confirmations.json; excluded from all baseline denominators and startup statistics.
methodology.sanitization: Allowlisted scalar metrics, labels, case IDs, HTTP status counts and manifest metadata only. No provider response URLs, media URLs, cookies, tokens, credentials or requested source hashes.

integrationReview.reason: The user supplied a current CineJoy watch page that appears fast and questioned whether the app integration uses outdated domains. The recorded baseline measures the deployed app integration, not the independent health or speed of the provider website. No fresh CineJoy results are included yet.
integrationReview.rankingDecision: Use currentDomainRetest for CineJoy. The original CineJoy attempts document the stale deployed integration, not current upstream reliability.

methodology.separation: These are selected-provider resume and endurance follow-ups. They never enter the 195 initial-start attempts, baseline success fractions or baseline first-frame percentiles.
methodology.resumeTiming: resumeTargetFrameMs is elapsed navigation-to-decoded-frame at the requested resume position, including resolution and seek. An earlier firstFrameMs is not proof of reaching the resume target.
methodology.coverage: Resume: two providers on all six titles at 300 seconds. Endurance: both providers on Shrek and Severance at 900 seconds. Selected matrices are complete; raw whole-inventory coverage is expected to be false.
methodology.quality: Decoded raster and media duration are observed. Shrek and Severance frame content was visually checked during the resume follow-up. No perceptual fidelity, track correctness, HDR or identical-cut claim is made.
methodology.stability: Steady-window deltas are separate event/frame counts. Waiting and stalled events are not added together. Null metrics on unsuccessful attempts are never zero-valued evidence.
methodology.selectionBias: Only the candidates with baseline playback were selected. The results confirm those candidates and are not extra comparative opportunities for the other sources.
methodology.sanitization: Scalar metrics, labels, HTTP statuses and source-file hashes only; private screenshots and provider URLs are excluded.

methodology.scope: Fresh app-integration retest. Keep these observations separate from the old-domain baseline and separate from interactive provider-site evidence.
methodology.availability: Every declared selected provider/title/round stays in the denominator. startedVideo requires a first decoded frame and matching requested source identity without fallback or identity mismatch. A later video reset can make final dimensions unknown without erasing a proven start. fullPlaybackPass mirrors raw success and additionally requires the continuous/steady checks. Starting video is not the same as passing the full playback check.
methodology.timing: Report startedTrialFirstFrame for all identity-verified starts, including attempts that later stalled, and fullPlaybackPassFirstFrame for attempts passing the full playback check. Synthetic-resume target-frame distributions are separate and require an observed target frame. Group each resume position separately and retain steady metrics independently. Never label full-playback pass counts as startup counts.
methodology.statistics: Each explicitly named subset gets its own median and observed nearest-rank p90 ceil(0.9*n), sample count and maximum. Missing metrics are null, never zero; small samples do not establish population uptime or tail latency.
methodology.matching: Reference comparisons require identical title, round, start mode, resume position and requested quality. A failed candidate/reference remains visible but has no paired timing difference.
methodology.requestedQuality: Record trial.requestedQuality and options.quality. If neither exists in an older run, infer legacy auto explicitly. Partition every summary by requested quality; a mismatch with the declared dataset quality invalidates eligibility. Forced 2160p/1080p/720p proof is separate from auto ranking evidence.
methodology.quality: Actual decoded width/height and captured manifest ladder declarations are distinct. Compare raster within a title; film cropping, letterboxing and tiny alignment differences must not become false quality scores. Advertised 4K/HDR does not prove decoded 4K/HDR or perceptual fidelity.
methodology.steady: Report requested and sampled window durations, advancing media time, waiting/stalled separately, and dropped/total frame deltas. Include started-trial observed steady totals so later buffering failures remain visible, alongside full-playback-pass-only totals. Label each window denominator; incomplete/missing windows are not fabricated as zeros. Do not add waiting and stalled events as independent interruptions.
methodology.provenance: Raw inputs are not modified. Verify supplied environment metadata names the actual retest runtime; checkout state is not deployment proof. Source filter affects whole-inventory coverage, not the declared selected matrix.
methodology.sanitization: Allowlisted metrics, labels, HTTP status counts and manifest width/height/bandwidth/codec/range declarations only. No provider/media URLs, credentials, cookies, auth material or requested source hashes.
methodology.ranking: No automatic ranking or deployment is performed. Review successful coverage, matched decoded quality, startup and stability before choosing a final operating policy.

coverage.note: A source-filtered run may fail the raw whole-inventory gate. It is usable only if every declared selected cell is present exactly once per round and identity/integrity checks pass.
